White dwarfs aren’t just white! Atmospheric gases reveal surprising hues like yellow, green, and purple.

https://t.co/1F1c8QzhAT

#StellarScience #WhiteDwarfs

urls.description: The universe hosts a myriad of star types, including supergiants, giants, main sequence, red dwarfs, brown dwarfs, white dwarfs, and neutron stars. What makes these stars stand out are just their sizes, but their colors, as each one hosts a distinct color based on their surface temperature, specifically orange, red, blue, and white based on cooler to hotter temperatures. While the correlation between star colors and surface temperatures has long been known throughout astronomy, what if star colors could change based on specific criteria, including their atmosphere?
urls.title: White Dwarfs Are Actually…Yellow, Green, Pink, and Purple?

JWST reveals lopsided exoplanet with blistering evening winds! Not a perfect sphere.

https://t.co/1BsCpWo3IX

#Exoplanets #JWST

urls.description: Typically, when we think of exoplanets, we think of neat spheres floating directly in front of their star, which acts as a giant spotlight. From our vantage point, they would look more like two perfect two dimensional circles than spheres, though. But nature is almost never so clean-cut. A new paper published in Nature Astronomy from researchers at Cornell and the University of Bristol details the first-ever study of an exoplanet that is noticeably lopsided.
urls.title: JWST Reveals a Lopsided Alien World with Blistering Evening Winds
